summary: Frontend-only verification of Axios mutation hardening across the 7 newly-hardened Patria pages (Council, MissionGoals, Dashboard, Household, SacredHeart, Settings, Today). Forced backend errors via Playwright page.route() for every required mutation; verified that NO React/Webpack error overlay appeared, NO 'Uncaught (in promise) AxiosError' was emitted to the console, and a readable Sonner toast was displayed. Modal/form state was preserved on failure and submit buttons were re-enabled. 0 uncaught promise rejections captured across all forced-error tests. Happy paths (Dashboard load, Council meeting start) still work normally.

Today.jsx mutations.reason: All three mutations (toggleRule, logPrayer, checkinChallenge) are wrapped in try/catch with toast.error(explainError(...)). However /today route in App.js redirects to /dashboard and Today.jsx is NOT imported anywhere in /app/frontend/src — the hardened module is dead code in the live app.

critical_code_review_comments: Today.jsx is hardened but unreachable: App.js redirects `/today` -> `/dashboard` and Today.jsx is not imported in any other file (grep across src/ returns no importers). The page-level hardening is correct (try/catch + toast.error(explainError)), but no user can ever exercise this code path. Recommend either (a) wiring Today.jsx into a real route, or (b) deleting the file to avoid confusion.

Council.jsx, MissionGoals.jsx, Household.jsx, SacredHeart.jsx, Settings.jsx, Dashboard.jsx all correctly follow the established pattern: import { toast } from 'sonner'; import { explainError } from '@/lib/errors'; every mutation wrapped in try/catch that calls toast.error(explainError(err, fallback)). explainError handles 401/403/404/Network gracefully and pulls server `detail` strings or Pydantic validation arrays.

Minor: Settings.jsx save button uses a `saving` flag for disable+text, but MissionGoals.jsx `Save mission` and Council finalize buttons are not disabled during the in-flight request — a fast double-click could fire two PATCH/POST calls. Not a regression for this hardening sweep, but worth tightening later.

Seed-data side-effect during testing: the first Household remove-button click in iteration 1 hit a non-primary member, which the backend accepted (200), reducing the Aquinas demo household from 3 -> 2 members. The hardening behavior was still verified correctly via a separate forced-400 in iteration 2. Recommend reseeding the third member if visual demo richness matters.
action_items: Decide fate of Today.jsx: either add a `<Route path="/today" element={<Today />} />` (and remove the existing redirect to /dashboard), or delete src/pages/Today.jsx and its hardening work. Currently it's dead code.
(Optional) Reseed the third Aquinas household member that was inadvertently removed during DELETE testing on /members.

(Optional polish) Add `saving` disabled flag to MissionGoals `Save mission`, Council `Finalize meeting`, and Council `Begin meeting` buttons for parity with Settings.jsx (the only page in this sweep that already does it).

context_for_next_testing_agent: All 7 hardened pages confirmed to surface axios errors via Sonner toasts with NO React/webpack error overlay and 0 uncaught promise rejections in console. Pattern: page.route('**/api/<endpoint>', fulfill 4xx/5xx) then trigger the mutation, then assert (a) no iframe[id^=webpack-dev-server], (b) no .react-error-overlay, (c) a [data-sonner-toast] is visible with human-readable text. SacredHeart.jsx lives at /spiritual?tab=sacred-heart (NOT a top-level route). Household.jsx is mounted as `Members` at /members. Today.jsx is currently dead code — /today redirects to /dashboard.
rca of the issue: N/A — verification task, no bugs found in the hardening sweep itself. Only finding is the architectural gap that Today.jsx hardening is unreachable in the running app.
